title: Video-Based Psychotherapy in Outpatient Psychotherapeutic Care - the Use of Virtual Reality
summary:
This study examines whether virtual reality exposure therapy (VRET) is feasible, acceptable, and tolerable for patients and their therapists in a real-life outpatient psychotherapeutic setting for short-term treatment of social phobia and agoraphobia with and without panic disorder. In addition, we examine preliminary effectiveness by comparing the change in anxiety symptoms with a control group that receives in-vivo exposure therapy (IVET) as part of short-term treatment. We will recruit 60 people with social phobia and/or agoraphobia with and without panic disorder at several study centers.
Both groups receive short-term behavioral therapy treatment over 12 50-minute individual sessions based on established treatment manuals and embedded in the exposure therapy sessions 6-10. In the intervention group (VRET), exposure takes place exclusively via virtual reality. The control group (IVET) receives exposure therapy in-vivo.
Measurement time points are before the start of therapy, immediately after an exposure session, and after the end of the twelfth session. We supplement well-founded qualitative data by asking therapists and patients about their experiences via questionnaires and interviews.
The main result is an evaluation of whether VRET triggers anxiety in the context of short-term therapy to treat social phobia and agoraphobia (with and without panic disorder) and how severe the anxiety symptoms are at the end of the intervention. In addition, we investigate to what extent VRET can be part of the regular outpatient psychotherapeutic short-term treatment of social phobia and agoraphobia (with and without panic disorder) and what advantages VRET has compared to IVET.

interventions.name: 12 sessions of short-term behavioral therapy, including exposures using Virtual Reality (VRET, in-virtuo), at study center Magdeburg
12 sessions of short-term behavioral therapy, including exposures in-vivo (IVET), at study centers Hannover and Berlin

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
diagnosed ICD-10 F40.0 or F40.01 and/or F40.1; insurance AOK Sachsen-Anhalt for study center Magdeburg
Exclusion criteria:
acute psychotic disorder, acute suicidality, alcohol or drug dependence, major cardiovascular disorder, mental disability, organic brain disorder, epilepsy
